summary: The 7th grade Glen Helen overnight camp requires a **$50 deposit by Friday, August 28, 2026** (total cost $165, balance $115). Students must submit both a **Commitment Letter** and **Discipline Contract** by this deadline. Additional paperwork (health form, photo waiver) and full payment are due by **Friday, September 11, 2026**. Medical permits must be turned in **three days before departure** with correct medication paperwork. The trip uses a **3-strike behavior system** at Glen Helen, with **no refund** if a child is removed for behavior. Starting **August 31st**, a similar behavior system applies at school leading up to the trip—a 3rd offense results in removal from the trip with full refund available prior to September 15, 2026, partial refund after. Students who receive in-school or out-of-school suspension will be immediately suspended from the trip. Payment options include cash, check (to Talawanda Middle School), or pie sale/cookie dough fundraiser earnings.

title: Engineering and Coding Club for Middle School
source_title: OFF AND RUNNING!! | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
ENGINEERING 

AND 

CODING 

CLUB ENGINEERING AND CODING CLUB

After school Engineering and Coding Club starts in September. This is a dynamic and engaging environment where students in 6-8th grade can explore the world of engineering and coding. Our club is designed for students who are interested in technology, problem-solving, and innovation. Two Miami University based clubs will be directing our engineering and coding activities this year. Kode2Learn is a student organization that organizes and runs events for kids in the Oxford area that promote teamwork and problem solving through the use of computer programming. SWE (Society of Women Engineers) organization's goal is to encourage our middle school students to consider engineering or computing as a career and provide activities related to engineering/coding.Engineering/Coding Club times - Schedule(After school until 3:30 p.m.)Engineering Focus: SWENext - Thursdays Sept. 17, 24, Oct. 1, 8, 15Coding/Programming Focus: Kode2Learn - Wednesdays Oct. 21, 28, Nov. 4, 11, 18See Mrs. Ruppert for club permission slips (Room 406).

summary: An after-school **Engineering and Coding Club** for students in grades 6-8 starts in September, running until 3:30 p.m. The club features two Miami University organizations: **SWE (Society of Women Engineers)** leads engineering activities on Thursdays (Sept. 17, 24, Oct. 1, 8, 15), and **Kode2Learn** leads coding/programming sessions on Wednesdays (Oct. 21, 28, Nov. 4, 11, 18). Students can pick up permission slips from Mrs. Ruppert in Room 406.

title: Older Americans Month Community BINGO
source_title: 4 Days and Counting! | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Every May, Older Americans Month recognizes the contributions of older adults, highlights aging trends, and reaffirms commitments to serve our older community members. The 2026 theme is “Champion Your Health”.Throughout the month of May, Oxford Seniors, Age-Friendly Oxford, and the Coalition for a Healthy Community, Oxford Area are partnering to highlight and offer programming focused on promoting physical, mental, and emotional health and well-being at all ages.You can participate by playing “Community BINGO” with us! It’s as easy as 1, 2, 3!1) Print your own or pick up a Community Bingo card at any of the following locations:Oxford Seniors, 922 Tollgate Dr., OxfordOxford Lane Library, 441 S. Locust St.The Knolls of Oxford, Clubhouse or Front DeskScripps Gerontology Center, 396 Upham Hall, on campus2) Every time you do something listed on the card, mark it off. The goal is to get “BINGO” as many times as possible. A “BINGO” is marking off any 5 squares in a straight line – either vertically, horizontally, or diagonally.3) Bring your completed BINGO card to the Intergenerational BINGO Party on Sun. May 31 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. at Oxford Seniors for prizes, snacks, and FUN! A PDF version of the BINGO card is attached to this message if you'd like to print one at home.

summary: May is **Older Americans Month** with the theme "Champion Your Health." Oxford Seniors, Age-Friendly Oxford, and the Coalition for a Healthy Community are hosting **Community BINGO** throughout May. Pick up a BINGO card at Oxford Seniors (922 Tollgate Dr.), Oxford Lane Library (441 S. Locust St.), or The Knolls of Oxford, complete activities listed on the card, and bring your completed card to the **Intergenerational BINGO Party on Sunday, May 31 from 3:00-5:00 p.m. at Oxford Seniors** for prizes and snacks. Get BINGO by marking off any 5 squares in a straight line (vertically, horizontally, or diagonally).
